headline: Big AI week as OpenAI claims AGI milestone with GPT-6 Astra, while MSFT surges 2.7% last night and PLS dips 2.1% today on lithium sector pressure.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped 2.68% last night — one of the portfolio's biggest movers. The catalyst was a combination of strong AI-driven revenue momentum and a big announcement: Microsoft will start breaking out Azure cloud revenue quarterly for the first time, giving investors much clearer visibility into how its AI bet is paying off. Markets loved it.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI closed up 1.61% today, riding the broader AI excitement sparked by this week's model launches from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. The ETF's underlying holdings in AI-exposed companies got a tailwind from the sector buzz, even though it's still sitting about 13% below what was paid in.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google rose 1.59% last night after a court rejected the US government's attempt to break up its ad tech business. That's a meaningful legal win — it removes a major overhang that had been weighing on the stock. Add in the launch of Gemini 3.8 Flash and Google staying relevant in the AI race, and the mood was positive.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS ticked up 0.42% today, tracking last night's strong US session where the S&P 500 rose 1.06% and the NASDAQ jumped 1.4%. A broad tech rally lifted the whole US market ETF.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.21% today — a quiet, steady session. As a diversified multi-asset fund it doesn't move dramatically on any single day, which is exactly the point.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.14% today — barely moved. Emerging markets have been subdued as investors continue to focus on the US AI story and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East keep risk appetite cautious.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara fell 2.12% today as the broader lithium sector came under renewed selling pressure. Multiple ASX lithium stocks — PLS, WC8, PMT, BRE — all dropped together, suggesting sector-wide sentiment rather than a Pilbara-specific issue. Lithium prices remain soft and the market is still waiting for a demand catalyst to turn things around.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 0.93% last night — a mild pullback with no major catalyst. The big GTA VI leak story (Rockstar broke its silence calling the leaks 'heartbreaking') created some noise but didn't materially move the stock. Still sitting at a loss overall; the thesis remains tied to major game releases.

watch_today.title: MSFT: AI momentum is real — hold and be patient
watch_today.detail: Microsoft surged 2.68% last night and is now up over 15% on your cost base. The Azure revenue transparency announcement is a big positive — the market now gets clearer numbers on how Microsoft's AI investment is actually translating to revenue. For a long-term holder this is exactly what you want to see. No reason to sell into strength; just hold and let the AI story keep playing out.

watch_today.title: PLS: Down 2.1% today — but the long-term story isn't broken yet
watch_today.detail: Pilbara dropped another 2.12% today and is now down nearly 25% on your cost base. This is painful, but today's fall was sector-wide (multiple lithium stocks fell together), not a Pilbara-specific shock. The long-term case — lithium demand from EVs and energy storage — is still intact, though it's taking longer to materialise than most expected. Sit tight unless your conviction in the lithium story has changed fundamentally.

watch_today.title: GXAI: AI week gave it a lift — hold, but be aware of the gap
watch_today.detail: GXAI bounced 1.61% today on the back of massive AI news this week (GPT-6, Gemini 3.8, Claude updates). That's encouraging, but you're still about 13% below your entry price. For a long-term AI thematic ETF, weeks like this — where the whole sector gets excited — are what you're investing for. No action needed; just let the theme develop.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Ad tech breakup bid fails — a real legal win
watch_today.detail: A US court rejected the government's attempt to force Google to break up its ad tech business. This removes a significant legal risk that had been hanging over the stock, and Google gained 1.59% last night. Combined with the Gemini 3.8 Flash launch keeping Google competitive in the AI race, the long-term picture looks solid. Hold confidently.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike looking likely — watch the AUD and your mortgage
watch_today.detail: Australia's economy grew 2.1% and the RBA governor has given a 'grim rates warning', with markets now pricing a rate hike as 'all but assured'. The Aussie dollar has already climbed above 0.72 USD on the back of this. If you have a variable rate mortgage, worth thinking about. For your portfolio, a stronger AUD slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO), though the effect is modest.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI leak news — don't read too much into it
watch_today.detail: Rockstar Games (owned by Take-Two) publicly called the GTA VI leaks 'heartbreaking', which got media attention. But the stock only dipped 0.93% last night and there's no sign of lasting damage. GTA VI is still coming, and that's the entire long-term bet with TTWO. Hold.

world.summary: The biggest global stories today centre on the escalating US-Iran war, with Iran firing missiles at Kuwait and Israel claiming control of a key Lebanese ridge, while the Trump administration pushes the Supreme Court to allow sweeping mail-in voting restrictions ahead of US midterms.

stories.title: Iran fires missiles and drones at Kuwait as US-Iran war escalates
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has launched missiles and drones at Kuwait as part of an ongoing military exchange with the United States. Trump has said the US strike campaign 'won't last long', but the conflict is actively spreading beyond Iran's borders. Kuwait sits at the heart of global oil infrastructure — any escalation there could spike energy prices worldwide, including what Australians pay at the bowser. Oil is already sitting at $91.62 USD per barrel.

stories.title: Israel claims 'operational control' of Lebanon's Ali Al Taher ridge
stories.why_it_matters: The Israeli military says it now has 'operational control' of the Ali Al Taher ridge in Lebanon — a strategically significant high ground in the ongoing Iran-linked conflict. This marks a significant expansion of Israeli ground operations in Lebanon and raises the stakes in an already volatile multi-front conflict involving Iran, Hezbollah, and now direct US strikes on Iran. The broader Middle East conflict shows no sign of winding down.

stories.title: Trump administration takes mail-in voting battle all the way to the Supreme Court
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has asked the US Supreme Court to urgently allow new restrictions on mail-in voting, including requiring proof of citizenship on ballot applications, ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The administration is also working to compile state-level citizen voter lists. Critics argue this is a deliberate strategy to suppress votes — particularly from minorities and young people who are less likely to have citizenship documents readily at hand. The Supreme Court's decision could reshape how tens of millions of Americans vote in November.

stories.title: US-Iran tensions: 'Heavy attack' as fire is exchanged
stories.why_it_matters: Beyond the Kuwait missile strike, broader US-Iran military exchanges are being described as a 'heavy attack' with fire being exchanged directly between US and Iranian forces. Trump has framed it as a limited campaign, but the situation remains fluid. Markets are watching closely — oil and gold have both ticked higher on the uncertainty, with gold now at a record $4,516 USD per ounce.

stories.title: Modern warfare lessons: What Ukraine and the Middle East mean for Western militaries
stories.why_it_matters: With two major conflicts now running simultaneously — Ukraine vs Russia and the US-Iran war — military analysts are drawing lessons about what modern warfare actually looks like: drone swarms, precision missiles, cyber operations, and the blurring of civilian and military targets. For Australia, which is in a period of major defence spending and strategic repositioning in the Indo-Pacific, these conflicts are live case studies that are directly shaping policy in Canberra.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was a strong one — S&P 500 up 1.06%, NASDAQ up 1.4% — driven by AI excitement and the Microsoft Azure announcement. The ASX had a quieter day, slipping marginally by 0.16%. The Aussie dollar is pushing above 0.72 USD on rising RBA rate hike expectations, and gold has hit a record high above $4,500 USD as investors seek safety amid Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Slight dip today — the ASX gave back a little ground despite the positive US lead. Resources weighed on the index.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Strong session last night — broad rally led by tech and AI stocks.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Outperformed the broader market last night as AI-related stocks surged on GPT-6 and Microsoft news.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar climbing as traders price in a near-certain RBA rate hike. A stronger AUD slightly reduces the value of your US holdings when converted back.

indicators.name: Gold (XAU)
indicators.note: Gold hitting record highs — investors buying safety as Middle East conflict intensifies.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil nudging higher on Iran-Kuwait tensions — any further escalation in the Gulf could push this significantly higher.

politics.summary: The dominant domestic story today is the RBA and interest rates — Australia's economy grew a solid 2.1%, which has economists and markets now calling a rate hike 'all but assured'. The RBA governor has given a blunt warning that there's still 'a job to do' on inflation. Meanwhile, commentators are pointing the finger at Labor for politicising the central bank's independence.

stories.title: RBA rate hike 'all but assured' after economy grows 2.1%
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's GDP grew 2.1% — stronger than expected — which has effectively sealed the deal on an upcoming RBA rate rise. When the economy grows this fast, the Reserve Bank worries inflation will stay stubbornly high, so it lifts interest rates to cool things down. For anyone with a variable-rate mortgage, this means higher repayments are likely coming. For investors, higher rates here in Australia can weigh on growth stocks and property.

stories.title: RBA governor warns 'job's not done' on inflation — more hikes flagged
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA chief has made it clear that inflation hasn't been beaten yet and the central bank still has 'a job to do' — code for more rate hikes are on the table. The Aussie dollar jumped above 0.72 USD partly on this news, as traders bet that Australian interest rates will stay higher for longer. This is the single biggest domestic financial story for most Australians right now.

stories.title: Don't blame the RBA for Labor's political incompetence
stories.why_it_matters: Commentary in The Australian argues that Labor has undermined the RBA's political independence — blaming the government for using the central bank as a political football while trying to look tough on inflation. This reflects a broader tension between the Albanese government and the Reserve Bank that has been simmering for months. The key question is whether the government's spending is actually making the RBA's inflation-fighting job harder.

stories.title: Aussie dollar edges above 0.72 as RBA hike bets build, US jobs data in focus
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian dollar has climbed to 0.7206 USD — its highest level in recent weeks — as markets price in near-certain RBA rate hikes. All eyes are now on tonight's US non-farm payrolls (jobs) data, which could move currency markets significantly. A strong US jobs number would boost the USD and potentially pull the AUD back; a weak number would do the opposite. Worth watching if you have US-denominated holdings.

ai.summary: This has been one of the biggest AI weeks in recent memory. OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra and claimed it marks the beginning of the 'AGI era' (AGI = Artificial General Intelligence, meaning AI that can do most human tasks). Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash. Anthropic and Meta also shipped updates. Then all the major AI services crashed simultaneously — highlighting just how much of the world now depends on these systems.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, declares 'Welcome to the AGI era'
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has officially launched GPT-6 Astra and declared it an 'AGI milestone' — meaning the company believes this model can now perform most human cognitive tasks at human level or better. OpenAI has been rolling it out carefully after its own safety team flagged that it has advanced cyber capabilities — meaning it could theoretically help bad actors conduct cyberattacks. This is the most significant AI model launch since ChatGPT itself. For investors in GOOG and MSFT (both racing to keep up), this week has been a pressure test — and both are responding with their own launches.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Flash to compete on coding and cost
stories.why_it_matters: Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash is specifically designed to beat OpenAI and Anthropic on coding tasks and to do it cheaper. This is important because coding is one of the highest-value AI use cases for businesses right now — and price competition means AI tools are becoming more accessible to smaller companies. For Google (GOOG in your portfolio), staying competitive in the AI race is essential to its long-term valuation.

stories.title: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini all went down simultaneously — along with Amazon Web Services
stories.why_it_matters: In a striking moment, ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Anthropic's Claude, and Amazon Web Services all experienced outages at roughly the same time. Thousands of users across the globe were locked out. This highlights a growing vulnerability: as businesses and individuals become more reliant on AI tools, these services are becoming critical infrastructure — and when they go down, the impact is felt broadly. It's also a reminder that cloud concentration risk (too much of the internet running through a handful of companies) is a real systemic issue.

stories.title: Jensen Huang, Sam Altman and Elon Musk warn G20 against heavy AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: At the G20 technology summit, Nvidia's Jensen Huang, OpenAI's Sam Altman, and Elon Musk all pushed back hard against heavy government regulation of AI, arguing it would stifle innovation. The G20 nations broadly agreed, backing a 'light-touch' approach to AI governance. For Australia, this matters because our AI policy is likely to follow the international consensus — meaning AI companies will mostly self-regulate for now, which is good for tech investors but keeps safety concerns unresolved.

stories.title: FDA opens a fast-track path for generative AI medical devices
stories.why_it_matters: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is launching a pilot program that lets AI-powered medical devices reach patients faster — before they've been fully authorised — if they meet certain criteria. This is a significant shift: previously, AI medical tools faced the same slow approval process as traditional medical devices. For the AI industry, it opens up healthcare as a major new commercial frontier. Think AI tools that diagnose cancer from scans, flag drug interactions, or triage emergency patients.

sport.summary: The Broncos sent departing prop Payne Haas out a winner in Round 27, thrashing the Bulldogs 34-20 in last night's opener. Tonight the Titans host the Dolphins at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast, with the Rabbitohs vs Roosters to follow. AFL finals selection news is also rolling in, with a Geelong selection shock and the Blues hit by injury.

stories.title: Broncos thrash Bulldogs 34-20, send Haas out a winner
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane put on one of the scores of the 2026 season — 34-20 over Canterbury at Accor Stadium — in what was a farewell game for star prop Payne Haas. It was described as the top score of the season so far for the Broncos. A big statement game heading into the finals stretch, and a fitting send-off for Haas. The Bulldogs confirmed four players will exit the club at season's end.

stories.title: Titans vs Dolphins tonight at Cbus Super Stadium — Gold Coast derby
stories.why_it_matters: It's local NRL tonight — the Gold Coast Titans host the Dolphins at Cbus Super Stadium from 6pm. NRL.com also revealed the Titans are in talks to play a future game in Las Vegas as part of a push to grow the game internationally. Kickoff is right when you're reading this, so get the stream up.

stories.title: Warriors lose Halasima, backline reshuffled for Saturday
stories.why_it_matters: The Warriors have lost Halasima from their team list for Saturday's clash against the Sea Eagles, forcing a backline reshuffle. With the finals race tightening, every personnel change matters. Warriors fans will want to check the revised lineup before kick-off at 3pm Saturday in Auckland.

stories.title: AFL finals teams: Geelong selection shock, Blues hit by injury, Swans make big call
stories.why_it_matters: AFL finals selections are in and there are some big talking points: Geelong have sprung a surprise with their team selection, Carlton (the Blues) are dealing with a significant injury concern in their squad, and the Sydney Swans have made a bold call with their lineup. With finals footy now underway, these decisions could define club seasons.

stories.title: Fremantle's double injury hurdle threatens finals run
stories.why_it_matters: Fremantle's AFL finals campaign is under serious threat with a double injury concern emerging — the Dockers could be without two key players as they navigate what analysts are calling a tricky 'Fraser v Ali' matchup challenge. Fox Sports rates it as a significant hurdle for Freo's flag ambitions heading into the finals.
